articles.topic: CSO September 2026 Residential Property Price Index, transaction medians and buyer affordability
articles.distinct_thesis: The 4.7% index increase shows prices still rising more slowly, while the separate €400,000 rolling transaction median translates into a €40,000 standard deposit and €90,000 four-times-income illustration rather than a universal home valuation.

claim_checks.claim: National RPPI growth was 4.7%, Dublin 3.9% and outside Dublin 5.4% in the year to September 2026.
The €400,000 national median implies a €40,000 deposit, €360,000 mortgage and €90,000 income under the standard first-time-buyer limits.
claim_checks.basis: 400,000 × 10% = 40,000; 400,000 - 40,000 = 360,000; 360,000 / 4 = 90,000. Central Bank limits and lender discretion are stated.

claim_checks.claim: New dwellings were 24.3% of 4,714 September filings and first-time buyers were 40.7%.
claim_checks.basis: 1,146 / 4,714 × 100 = 24.31%; 1,920 / 4,714 × 100 = 40.73%. Both described as same-month household purchase filings.

articles.topic: CSO Labour Force Survey Q3 2026 record employment, underemployment and unemployment duration
articles.distinct_thesis: Record employment and lower unemployment coexist with 130,200 underemployed part-time workers and rising long-term unemployment, so employment status alone does not establish household income security.

claim_checks.claim: Employment reached 2,884,100, up 58,700 or 2.1%; unemployment was 150,700 and 5.0%.
claim_checks.basis: CSO Labour Force Survey Q3 2026 published 19 November at 11:00.

claim_checks.claim: 130,200 of 578,200 part-time workers were underemployed, equal to 22.5%.
claim_checks.basis: CSO key findings and employment table; underemployment is explicitly defined as wanting more hours for more pay.

claim_checks.claim: Long-term unemployment rose 2,600 or 7.6% to 37,100 while total unemployment fell.
claim_checks.basis: CSO unemployment duration section; long-term rate remained 1.2% and share excluding not-stated was 25.5%.

articles.topic: New CSO linked data on school pupils and household supports, with current BSCFA and Working Family Payment checks
articles.distinct_thesis: The newly published 2022 linked data demonstrate how school households depend on overlapping income, caring and disability supports, while a current-rules service layer prevents the historical 25.7% BSCFA finding being misreported as a 2026 caseload.

claim_checks.claim: 25.7% of pupils benefited from BSCFA in 2022; the rate was 67.2% in one-parent families and 16.8% in two-parent families.
claim_checks.basis: CSO Frontier Series release published 19 November 2026; article repeatedly identifies the data year and at-least-one-payment definition.

claim_checks.claim: 2026 BSCFA rates were €160 for ages 2–11 and €285 for ages 12–22, subject to conditions; the application window is closed.
claim_checks.basis: Department of Social Protection 2026 service page and operational guidelines; 18–22 coverage is restricted to return to full-time second-level education.

claim_checks.claim: A two-child family with €700 assessed weekly income would have an illustrative WFP calculation of €99.60 at the €866 limit.
claim_checks.basis: (866 - 700) × 60% = 99.60. Article states Department rounding and detailed assessment rules determine payment.
